text:
sara: Heads up — support ticket #12345 from Acme reports sudden p95/p99 spikes on embeddings API since last night. They see 4-6x tail latency, manifests in eu-west.

matt: seeing cluster-wide p99 bump on /v1/embeddings too. Started ~02:10 UTC after the CUDA15 + driver rollout. Correlating with node reboots and GPU firmware upgrades on fleet.

priya: confirmed. Alerts show host io wait and nvme queue depth climbing on upgraded hosts. I have a quick top + iostat snippet in the node pool: 
```
r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
10.0 5.0 2000 1500    35.0    2.3    12.5   1.2    11.3  0.90   92.1
```

akshat: interesting — NVMe %util at 92% on some nodes. Could be firmware IO path change interacting with our host kernel IO scheduler after driver update.

sara: customer says errors increased (502s) when embeddings timeouts hit. Support reports retries cascade and billing alarms triggered for high tail cost.

support-sre: ticket notes: 2026-03-16T02:18Z spike; customer observed 10s p99 on small embed requests (should be <300ms). They've sampled traces showing long wait in host_block_io.

matt: can we triage whether it's storage hotness (background NVMe GC/firmware) vs new GPU driver causing more memory pressure -> more IO flushes? Any recent kernel config changes in the rollout? @oncall-bot what deployments touched eu-west last 24h?

oncall-bot: deploys affecting eu-west in last 24h: CUDA15-driver v2.1.4 -> rolled 00:50-02:00 UTC; GPU firmware 1.3.7 -> staggered 01:10-03:00 UTC; kernel backport kexec patch not in eu-west.

priya: I pushed a quick query across affected nodes: most high-io hosts also have firmware 1.3.7 + new driver. Baseline hosts (old firmware) show normal p99. Also seeing increased KV-cache writeback spikes correlating with model cache flushes.

akshat: mitigation ideas: 1) Pin traffic off affected nodes via routing (evict pods, cordon nodes). 2) Rollback driver on a small canary set. 3) Adjust qdisc/cgroups to deprioritize background GC. 4) Temporary model routing fallback to smaller model variant for customers.

sara: prioritize: (A) divert production embeddings traffic away from affected node-pool, (B) enable temporary batch-size throttle to reduce burst IO, (C) open rollback plan for driver/firmware if divert doesn't help.

matt: I'm starting the node cordon/evict for eu-west-pool-b now — will route traffic to eu-west-pool-a (older firmware). Taking subset: 10 nodes first. Command: 
```
kubectl cordon node-12-eu-west-1
kubectl drain node-12-eu-west-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

priya: added a temporary route rule to RT router to avoid pool-b. Also reduced max inference batch size from 32 -> 8 for embeddings route to lower IO pressure.

oncall-bot: routing rule applied. 10 nodes cordoned/evicted. Autoscaler will bring up replacements in pool-a if needed.

support-sre: customer updated: latency improved to p99 ~600ms from 10s after traffic shift. They still see occasional spikes but the error rate dropped by 80%.

akshat: good signal. Next: we should capture kernel traces and nvme firmware logs from an affected host before we repro. I opened an internal bug with vendor and attached logs: BUG-2026-88.

matt: agreed — we should prepare rollback playbook for driver and firmware. If rollback needed: (1) pause rollout, (2) pin nodes to previous driver image, (3) do controlled restart. I'll draft steps.

sara: capture action items: 
- Priya: keep routing and batch throttle in place until root cause confirmed.
- Matt: rollback playbook + coordinate with infra-ops for firmware vendor support.
- Akshat: collect block traces + nvme SMART + dmesg from affected nodes and attach to BUG-2026-88.
- Support-sre: update customer with mitigation progress and offer credits if SLA breach confirmed.

priya: noted. I'll leave route in place and run a 2h watch on p95/p99. If stable, start gradual uncordon of nodes one-by-one with health checks.

support-sre: I'll keep ticket updated. Customer appreciates quick routing fix; wants root cause timeline.

sara: thanks team. We'll reconvene if p99 goes above 1s or errors > baseline. Filing incident follow-up doc and postmortem checklist.

akshat: FYI: I also found a host kernel IO reclaim parameter that was at default; increasing vm.dirty_ratio on a test node reduced writeback bursts. Might be a short-term knob while vendor investigates.

matt: good call — but be careful global knobs affect all. Test-only first.

sara: closing loop for now. If anyone sees a regression when we uncordon, @channel ping immediately with tracestate. :thumbsup:
